subject: Hosted API: p99 spike investigation & SDK timeout behavior
messages:
From: Grace Hopper <grace@fintechco.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: support@fintechco.com
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Intermittent high tail latency (p95/p99) since 2/17 affecting checkout flows

Hi Sergio,

We started seeing intermittent spikes in p95/p99 latency on the Redwood Hosted API starting ~2026-02-17 19:00 UTC. The spikes are concentrated on our payment/checkout route and have caused several client-side SDK timeouts. Our logs show the SDK retry logic is firing repeatedly which is compounding load and causing downstream 5xxs. Attaching a trimmed trace and some request ids: req_6b9f2a, req_6b9f2b, req_6b9f2c.

Impact: increased checkout latency, a few failed orders, and user-facing errors (30–45 minute intermittent window).

We assume this is an API-side regression (p99 from ~380ms to ~1.6s). Can you confirm whether Redwood saw backend p99/p95 regressions and if there are mitigation steps? We need an ETA — our execs are asking.

Attaching: fintechco-traces-0218.log (relevant spans and SDK timestamps).

Thanks,
Grace Hopper
Head of Platform Reliability
FinTechCo

Internal triage notes (summary) — sending raw notes for transparency: 

1) Short timeline: around 2026-02-17T18:50–19:30 UTC we saw a cluster of elevated p99s on the hosted text-generation path used by FinTechCo. The service team observed brief backend CPU pressure on a subset of nodes but not a full cluster outage.

2) Crucial observation: many of the customer-side traces show client-side timeouts and immediate SDK retries. The SDK telemetry (attached) reports a higher-than-expected retry rate starting 2026-02-17 18:40 UTC that aligns exactly with FinTechCo's observed window.

3) Correlation vs causation: raw host-side latencies rose ~20–30% for certain request shapes but do NOT fully explain the multiplicative effect in FinTechCo's traces. The amplification looks like a retry storm initiated by aggressive client-side timeouts and an SDK backoff implementation change in SDK v2.3.1 (released 2026-02-15).

4) Root cause hypothesis: a recent SDK change adjusted the default socket/read timeout upward but changed the retry backoff math (bug introduced in v2.3.1). Some clients with short custom timeouts retried before the server-side request completed, producing overlapping requests and increasing server-side queueing and p99. In short: client retries produced the majority of the visible tail amplification.

5) Immediate mitigations implemented (today):
- Roll back the problematic backoff code from SDK v2.3.1 for hosted SDK endpoints (temporary pin to v2.3.0 behavior).
- Enable per-account gentle rate limiting (10% reduction window) for FinTechCo to allow traces to drain without impacting correctness.
- Turn on stricter server-side idempotency token validation and reject obvious duplicate rapid retries with 409s instead of processing them.

6) Next steps / owner map:
- Engineering (Jordan) will validate rollback metrics and confirm p99 trend within 2 hours.
- CS (Monica) will coordinate a post-mortem meeting with FinTechCo and share recommended SDK config knobs.
- Product (Sergio) will propose a short mitigation/FAQ doc for customers about timeout/retry settings.

Attachments: sdk-telemetry-heap.csv (sampling of SDK retry counters), server-snap-0218.log (short traces).

I'll post an incident summary and timeframe to customers after engineering confirms the rollback effect.

Hi Grace — follow-up and summary after our triage: 

Thank you again for the traces you provided — they were critical. Our post-triage findings: 
- Primary cause: an interaction between FinTechCo's client-side timeout configuration and an unintended change in SDK v2.3.1 retry/backoff behavior. The SDK change made some clients issue retries earlier than before; those retries overlapped with in-flight server requests and amplified tail latencies.
- Secondary contributors: a minor transient CPU pressure on a handful of nodes at the same time. That alone would not have produced the scale of p99s you observed.

What we did: 
- Rolled back the transient backoff change to restore prior retry semantics (complete at ~2026-02-18T15:20 UTC).
- Applied temporary per-account rate dampening for your traffic profile while we validated results.
- Implemented server-side duplicate detection for rapid retry bursts (sending 409s for short-window duplicates) to prevent amplification.

Current status: p95/p99 for your routes are back within acceptable bounds (p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 620ms) based on 24h of samples. We've attached the incident summary.

Recommended actions for FinTechCo:
- If you run custom client-side timeouts, increase read timeout by 50% for 48 hours while we finish a robust SDK patch (target: v2.3.2) with safer default backoffs.
- Upgrade to the patched SDK (we will publish v2.3.2 tomorrow) which includes the rollback and additional telemetries to detect early retry storms.

Next steps: Monica will schedule a detailed post-mortem and we'll provide a short joint customer-facing FAQ.

Apologies again for the disruption. Let me know if you'd like an exec-level summary or a call with engineering leads.

Regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
